sentences.text: 4. Heard Sri Abhishek Srivastava, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Anil Kumar, learned counsel for the first informant, Sri Sri Bade Lal Bind, learned counsel for the State and perused the material on record.

5. This bail application under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed by the applicant-Vijay Kumar Singh Beriya, seeking enlargement on bail during trial in connection with Case Crime No.156 of 2020, under Sections 342, 506, 376 I.P.C., registered at Police Station Kharela, District Mahoba.

6. The FIR of the matter was lodged on 27.12.2020 by the victim herself against the applicant and Santosh Singh on the basis of application given to the I.G. Police, Chitrakoot Dham, Division Banda with the allegation that she was married to Veer Singh of Hameerpur.
She is working in the social welfare department and used to visit villages in ceremonies.

On 8.12.2020 at about 7 p.m. she had gone to Mahoba where she met the applicant who took her to his house and by threatening her with a country-made pistol confined her therein for three days and committed rape upon her.
He did not allow her to go out.
She told about it to his brother Santosh Singh but he also threatened her and stated that if she goes out, she would be murdered.

The mother of the applicant then came there who was also told of her grievance who also did not let her go out and then she cut her hand and placed the knife on her neck and threatened that if she is not permitted to go, she would cut her neck and commit suicide on which their mother told to both the persons to let her go otherwise they would get trapped and then the applicant dropped her on outskirts of the village on 12.12.2020 after committing rape upon her and ran away.
He also made an objectionable video of the act and was blackmailing her and telling her to keep her forcibly as his wife.
He threatened her of forcibly kidnapping her on 22.12.2020.
She gave an application at police station but no action was taken.
She then moved the said application on which various orders were passed and then FIR has been lodged.
7. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.

While placing para no.13 of the affidavit, it is argued that the applicant had applied for anticipatory bail before this Court which was granted to him till submission of police report under Section 173 Cr.P.C. vide order dated 22.3.2021.

While placing para no.19 of the affidavit, it is argued that the applicant is a soldier posted in the Indian Army at the post of Armourer in 14 Core Signal Regiment and at the time of incident was posted in Laddakh and was performing his duty in Indian Army.
While placing para no.17 of the affidavit, it is argued that the first informant was earlier in relationship with Santosh Singh, the elder brother of the applicant and wanted to marry him.
She used to live in the house with him as his wife.

The first informant is highly ambitious lady and wanted to marry the elder brother of the applicant but when she met the applicant and came to know about the applicant and his service and money, she wanted to marry with him which was refused by the applicant then she demanded money and land from him and after the same was refused, the present FIR has been lodged.
It is argued that no objectionable video has been recovered during investigation.

The charge sheet in the matter has been submitted against the applicant under Section 376, 342, 506 IPC whereas the same has been submitted against co-accused Santosh Kumar Singh Beriya under Sections 342, 506 IPC and 66-E of the Information Technology (Amendment) Act, 2008.

It has also been pointed out that the applicant is not having any criminal Vijay Kumar Singh Beriya vs State Of U.P. on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/43736696/
2 history as stated in para 4 of the affidavit and is in jail since 28.7.2023.

sentences.text: 8. Per contra learned counsel for the first informant and learned counsel for the State vehemently opposed the prayer for bail and argued that the applicant is involved in the present case as he is named in the FIR and there are allegations of detaining the first informant in his house under threat and committing rape upon her.

It is argued that even the averment in the FIR regarding the first informant cutting her hand with a knife at the house of the applicant gets corroborated from her medical report in which the doctor in her upper limb found six incissonal mark present over the right fore arm.
The applicant has absconded in the matter after lodging of the FIR.

He after anticipatory bail was granted to him, charge sheet in the matter was submitted on which the court concerned took cognizance challenged the same before this Court and an order dated 6.12.2021 was passed by a coordinate Bench of this Court in Application U/S 482 No.20022 of 2021 (Vijay Kumar Singh Beriya Fauji Vs. State of U.P. and another) in which he was granted two weeks' time to surrender before the trial court and apply for bail but he did not do so and absconded.

entities.text: Vijay Kumar Singh Beriya Fauji Vs. State of U.P. and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is argued that the first informant filed an application being Application U/S 482 No.27323 of 2022 (Sonam Singh Vs. State of U.P.) before this Court for a direction to the C.J.M. concerned for completing formalities in the matter without unreasonable delay which was disposed of directing the Superintendent of Police, Mahoba to take all the necessary endeavour to execute the non-bailable warrant on the accused vide order dated 30.9.2022.

entities.text: Sonam Singh Vs. State of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Subsequently even then the non-bailable warrants were not executed upon which the Contempt Application (Civil) No.944 of 2023 (Sonam Singh Vs. Sudha Singh, S.P) was filed before this Court in which an affidavit of the respondent was filed stating therein that communication is being done with the Army for service of the NBW upon the applicant, the same was recorded in the order dated 19.7.2023.

entities.text: Contempt Application (Civil) No.944 of 2023 (Sonam Singh Vs. Sudha Singh, S.P)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Subsequently the applicant surrendered on 28.7.2023.

There are good chances of the applicant again absconding in the matter if he is released on bail.
9.

After hearing the counsel for the parties and perusing the record, it is apparent that the applicant is named in the FIR, in the statement of the first informant under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. and there are allegations against him of committing rape upon her after getting her in confinement.

The applicant despite knowing of the present case and implication as is evident that he had applied for anticipatory bail which was allowed to him till conclusion of investigation after which charge sheet was submitted which was subjected to challenge by him in which an order was passed for him to surrender within two weeks did not comply with the same and kept on absconding from 2021 to 2023.
It was with great difficulty that he surrendered.
He being an employee of a disciplined force was not expected to not obey the orders of Court.

10. Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, conduct of the applicant, nature of allegations and medical examination report of the victim, I do not find it a fit case for bail, hence, the bail application is rejected.
